title: Lines Not Crossed
style: Folk-rock, yonna or chichamaya percussion opens alone before kasha drums join gaita macho and gaita hembra, with drum kit, electric guitars and electric bass; wide layered guitar tracks and tight percussion; mixed lead-and-chorus vocals build through the pre-choruses into a fuller final chorus; steady midtempo backbeat.
lyrics:
[Intro]
Zahra comes to La Guajira with family at her side
To see the project Thomas built where desert meets the tide

[yonna or chichamaya percussions solo]

[Verse 1]
The waves roll in on golden sand
Where Thomas stands and speaks
Of pages turned and meanings deep
That still his silence seeks

Zahra sits with Jan-Alan
Her husband close at hand
She speaks of passing romance days
She struggled to understand

[Pre-chorus]
The shore holds what the years let slip
And what she never could equip

[Chorus]
Healing from the mistakes we made
The lines we drew, the debts we paid
Two hearts that learned to let go free
What couldn't be, what couldn't be
The past is past, the wound is sealed
And what was broken now is healed

[Verse 2]
The council buzzes, words are thrown
Debate on either side
Old pütchipü'üi holds the floor
Though screens illuminate

Zahra rests her hand on him
As desert light grows dim
"One silver lining—I stayed true
And did not cross the line to you"

[Pre-chorus]
Tradition stands though time moves on
What served the past still carries on

[Chorus]
Healing from the mistakes we made
The lines we drew, the debts we paid
Two hearts that learned to let go free
What couldn't be, what couldn't be
The old and new can coexist
And what was broken now is healed

[Bridge]
He signals to his security
And makes a detour purposely
They park where desert meets the sky
And look into each other's eyes
"We are not going all the way"
A kiss that almost makes them stay

[Final Chorus]
Healing from the mistakes we made
The lines we drew, the debts we paid (the lines we drew)
Two hearts that learned to let go free (let go free)
What couldn't be, what couldn't be (couldn't be)
Transgression held in self-restraint
And what was broken now is healed (now is healed)
What was broken now is healed
